reasoning: Paf1 is a core subunit of the PAF1 transcription‑elongation complex that promotes Pol II pause release and deposition of activating histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K36me3) at many immune‑responsive promoters. There is no evidence that Paf1 directly binds the Fcgr2b promoter, but Fcgr2b is an NF‑κB/STAT‑responsive gene whose transcription in LPS‑stimulated BMDMs depends on efficient elongation. Loss of Paf1 therefore impairs the transcriptional activation of such targets, leading to reduced Fcgr2b mRNA levels.
